LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 2.1.2 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.1: Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 2.1.2 Conversational skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 2.1.2 Conversational skills, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why does the proper articulation of signs or sounds matter? 2. How do idea connectors affect the flow of conversations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 2.1.2 Conversational skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: The learner carries out research as they look for examples of idea connectors in books or the internet.

● Self-efficacy: The learner displays attention to detail as they watch a video and note how speakers start, end or change a

topic during a conversation.

Values:
● Patriotism: The learners exercise dedication when they collaboratively practise changing a topic and ordering ideas during

mock speeches.

● Unity: The learner avoids discrimination as they collaboratively recite poems or form minimal pairs in words with the

letter sounds / ə /, /ɑ: / and / ɜ: /.
